title: A continuous field of force shapes the whole organism regardless of its cells

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A continuous field of force shapes the whole organism regardless of its cells

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The multicellular organism is not a colony of independent cells: a continuous field of force runs through the entire organism, not restricted to protoplasmic continuity, and shapes it independently of the number, size and form of its cells.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And such a continuous field of force, somehow shaping the whole organism, independently of the number, magnitude and form of the individual cells, which enter, like a froth, into its fabric, seems to me certainly and obviously to exist.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Organism dominates cell formation”. Scope: multicellular plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern tissue mechanics and morphogen fields provide measurable partial interpretations. The strong independence from cell number, size, and form is difficult to isolate, and the historical concept admits several non-equivalent operationalizations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map tissue-scale stress or morphogen fields together with cell number, size, and shape during morphogenesis, then test whether organismal form remains predictable after those cellular variables are perturbed or controlled. Evidence of long-range patterning robust to cellular rearrangement supports a restricted field interpretation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Field of force' can mean mechanics, signaling, or an abstract pattern.

Tissue fields are generated and transmitted by cells, complicating independence.

Whole-organism matched perturbations are sparse.

fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.65
analysis feasibility: 0.4
operationalizability: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Independence of overall form from cell number is a testable fragment, and it has been studied in a few model organisms whose descriptions can be compiled. MorphoSource supplies shape, not the cell counts. The stronger wording, a continuous force field running through the whole organism, is not separated by those data from ordinary intercellular coordination.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare organismal shape in cases where cell number, cell size or cell form is altered, and ask whether the outline is unchanged. Shape that is invariant to cell number would support independence from the cellular partition; shape that scales with the cell grid would refute it. A continuous force field, as against cell-cell signalling, is not identified by that invariance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cell-number and cell-size series are not attached to most scans.

The field is said to be unrestricted by protoplasmic continuity, which is not a column in morphological databases.

Signalling across cells can coordinate form without a continuous physical field.
